holidays.name: National Pepperoni Pizza Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the undisputed king of pizza toppings, those spicy, slightly greasy red discs that curl into tiny grease-filled cups when baked. Pizzerias across the US roll out deals and pizza lovers argue over whether cup-and-char is the superior pepperoni style.
holidays.origin: Pepperoni Pizza Day is an unofficial food holiday that grew out of the American food-marketing and social media calendar. Pepperoni itself is an Italian-American invention, developed by Italian immigrants in the early 20th century, and it has no direct counterpart in Italy.
holidays.funFact: The word 'peperoni' in Italian actually means bell peppers, so if you order a 'pepperoni pizza' in Italy, you will get a pizza topped with peppers rather than spicy salami.

holidays.name: National Punch Day
holidays.description: A day to raise a glass of fruity, festive punch, whether it is a spiked bowl at a party or a nostalgic fruit punch from childhood. It is a perfect excuse to dust off the big punch bowl and tiny ladle.
holidays.origin: Punch Day is an unofficial food and drink observance. The drink itself traces back to 17th-century India, where British sailors and East India Company traders adapted a local drink made with five ingredients.
holidays.funFact: The word 'punch' likely comes from the Hindi word 'panch,' meaning 'five,' referring to the traditional five ingredients: alcohol, sugar, lemon, water, and tea or spice.

holidays.name: National Rum Punch Day
holidays.description: A tropical twist on the punch celebration, dedicated to the sweet, citrusy, and dangerously smooth blend of rum, juice, and spice. Cue the paper umbrellas and the beach-vacation daydreams.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial drink holiday celebrated by cocktail fans and bars, rooted in Caribbean traditions where rum punch is practically a national treasure.
holidays.funFact: A famous Caribbean rhyme guides the recipe: 'One of sour, two of sweet, three of strong, four of weak,' meaning lime juice, sugar, rum, and water or juice in those ratios.

holidays.name: Talk Like a Pirate Day Adjacent: Pirate-Themed Chaos Day (Approx.)
holidays.description: This is the day before International Talk Like a Pirate Day, when landlubbers around the world start practicing their 'arrrs,' brushing up on pirate slang, and hunting for their parrot costumes.
holidays.origin: International Talk Like a Pirate Day was started in 1995 by John Baur and Mark Summers of Oregon after a racquetball game, and it spread when humorist Dave Barry wrote about it in 2002.
holidays.funFact: Talk Like a Pirate Day is on September 19 because Baur's ex-wife's birthday was that date, which made it easy for him to remember.

holidays.name: National Fruit Cocktail Day Adjacent: Fall of the Fruit Punch Bowl
holidays.description: A playful reminder that the punch bowl season is in full swing as the weather turns toward fall. Gather friends, add some floating fruit slices, and enjoy a vintage-style party.
holidays.origin: This is a lighthearted unofficial observance that builds on the punch-themed celebrations of the date, rooted in classic mid-century party culture.
holidays.funFact: Punch bowls were once so fashionable in 18th-century England that elaborate silver and porcelain bowls were commissioned to hold hundreds of servings, and some were large enough to hold a small child.
